Hi Samantha (and team),

Thanks for the concrete examples — below is the exact accounting behavior applied by Redwood Hosted API (current public rate-card behavior). I'll keep it to the concrete math so procurement can model.

Principles (short):
- All message content passed to the model in a request is charged as input tokens (system, assistant, user, tool inputs that are fed into the model).
- Anything the model emits as a response in that same API call is charged as output tokens.
- If text produced by a tool is subsequently sent back to the model in a separate API call, it will be charged again as input tokens in that subsequent call. There is no automatic deduplication across requests.
- Rounding: we round token counts up to the next whole token at the per-request level (we count tokens as integers; there is no fractional token billing). We do not round per-batch across multiple HTTP calls.
- Prefix/KV caching: when we serve repeated prefixes from our KV cache, you are not charged for tokens served from cache on the model execution path. However, there is a separate small cache-hit accounting metric for some cache tiers — for hosted customers, cache hits reduce compute usage and thus the effective billed tokens. For procurement modeling assume conservative no-cache.

Concrete examples (using your spreadsheet rows):

A) Single chat call (one API request)
- System: 40 input tokens
- User: 60 input tokens
- Model generates: 300 output tokens

Billing: Input = 40 + 60 = 100 tokens charged at input rate
Output = 300 tokens charged at output rate
Rounding: Each of the above token sums are integers already; total tokens billed = 100 input + 300 output. If model produced 300.7 internally, we charge 301 output tokens (per-request rounding up).

B) Chat with tool call flow (tool invoked synchronously within same request vs asynchronous):
Scenario 1 (synchronous tool result returned to model inside same API call):
- System: 40 input tokens
- User: 30 input tokens
- Model calls tool; tool returns 120 tokens which are fed back into the model within the same request; model emits 180 output tokens to the client

Billing for single request (everything inside one API call):
- Input tokens: 40 (system) + 30 (user) + 120 (tool content passed into model) = 190 input tokens
- Output tokens: 180 (final model output to client)

Total billed (per-request rounding applies where needed): input 190 + output 180. There is no double-charge because the tool data was part of the same request and counted once as input.

Scenario 2 (tool result returned to client, then re-submitted in a separate new request to the model):
- Request 1 (tool call): you are billed for the request that generated the tool content (if that request involved model generation, those output tokens were billed as output).
- Request 2 (model receives the tool content as new input): when you resubmit that tool content to the model in a new HTTP call, those tokens are billed again as input tokens for Request 2. So they are billable twice across two separate requests.

Notes on edge cases:
- System/tool tokens included in prompt engineering templates (e.g., long system prompts) are always input tokens. If you store a large system prompt server-side and reuse it via the client without repeatedly sending it, you avoid repeated input charges — but in Hosted API the prompt must be sent with the request unless you use our managed prompts feature (which has its own accounting; we can provide details).
- We don't currently apply any per-minute amortized rounding — every HTTP request is independently tokenized and rounded up to the next integer.

If you want, I took your spreadsheet and produced a few sample invoice lines with list-price math and the discount bands Marissa manages; I uploaded the sample sheet to the Drive link in Jonas's thread. Happy to jump on a 30-min call with procurement if that helps finalize assumptions.
